chunks: There is no good in much of their secret counsel, except for him who commands charity or goodness or reconciliation between people; and whoever does so seeking the pleasure of God, We shall give him a great reward.
ai.seo_question: What makes secret counsel good or bad according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse distinguishes between general private conversations, which may be frivolous or secretive, and those with divine purpose, specifically charity (sadaqah), goodness (ma'ruf), and reconciliation (islah). The emphasis on 'seeking God's pleasure' (ibtigha'a mardat Allah) underscores the importance of intention (niyyah) in validating these acts, a core principle in Shia jurisprudence and spirituality. It serves as a moral guideline for social interactions, encouraging believers to transform private discourse into opportunities for spiritual and communal benefit.
